events.title: Clean up when app-server initialization fails
events.body:
Wrap the initialize call and initialized notification in exception handling that closes the selector and terminates and waits for the child before re-raising the original exception. The current constructor exits on an initialization timeout, RPC error, or write failure without calling close(), potentially leaving an app-server process running. Critic pass: cleanup can itself fail and hide the diagnostic; the revised change must preserve the original initialization exception.
Use mocked subprocess and selector objects with no network. Force initialize to raise a known exception, then assert that the selector is closed, the child is terminated and waited for, and the same exception reaches the caller. Repeat with cleanup raising an exception to verify that the initialization error remains visible. The claim is falsified if the existing constructor already performs this cleanup or if the proposed regression fails.
Cleanup must tolerate a child that has already exited and partially initialized resources. Keep existing live model defaults unchanged.

events.title: Clean up resources when initialization fails
events.body:
Ji An: Wrap the initialize call and initialized send in exception cleanup that closes the selector, terminates and reaps the child, then re-raises the original exception. Evidence: either operation can raise after resource creation; the supplied constructor has no cleanup path. Critic pass: cleanup can itself fail, so preserve the original initialization exception. Keep model defaults unchanged.
Add deterministic, network-free tests using fake process, selector, and transport objects. Inject an initialize timeout and an initialized-send failure separately. Assert selector closure, child termination and reaping, and propagation of the original exception. Include a successful handshake that performs no cleanup. Falsifier: either failure already releases these resources in the supplied implementation, or the revised implementation fails any assertion. Tests proposed, not executed.
Cleanup could mask the triggering error or delay failure reporting. Preserve the original exception and use the existing bounded terminate/wait/kill sequence. This fixes failed-construction cleanup; it does not establish broader diagnostic reliability.

events.title: Distinguish RPC responses from server requests
events.body:
The supplied call() accepts any message with the matching id as its response. A server request with that id and a method would prematurely return None. Change response recognition to require a JSON object, the matching id, no method, and exactly one of result or error; preserve other messages through the existing unmatched-message path. Keep live model defaults unchanged.
Proposed deterministic, offline regression: use a fake transport that delivers a server request {"id":1,"method":"example/request","params":{}} followed by {"id":1,"result":{"ok":true}}. Assert call() returns {"ok":true} and retains the request. The current implementation returns None. The defect claim is falsified if the unchanged implementation passes this fixture; the proposed fix fails if it drops the request or misses the real response.
Additional observed limits: read() buffers unterminated frames without a size bound, malformed JSON escapes without diagnostic context, and EOF discards any partial frame. call() also imposes a 0.1-second minimum read timeout that can exceed its remaining budget. These are separate follow-ups. No tools or tests were run; conclusions use only the supplied source.

events.title: Reject malformed JSON-RPC lines with useful diagnostics
events.body:
In `app/codex_rpc.py`, catch `json.JSONDecodeError` in `read()` and raise a `RuntimeError` that identifies the malformed line (or its safe, bounded representation) and preserves the parse exception as its cause. Today a malformed stdout line leaks a parser exception without clarifying that the app-server protocol response was invalid. This is a small diagnostic improvement; avoid including unbounded output in the error.
Use a fake app-server subprocess that writes a malformed JSON line, then a newline. Assert `read()` raises the protocol-specific error promptly and that its cause is `json.JSONDecodeError`. The test is deterministic and uses no network.
This only improves malformed-response diagnostics; it does not change valid RPC behavior. The claim is falsified if the existing exception already identifies the invalid app-server response clearly, or if the proposed regression cannot distinguish the new diagnostic from the current raw parse failure.

events.title: Clean up after initialization failure
events.body:
No initial proposal was supplied to assess. Source-backed defect: after spawning the server and registering stdout, __init__ calls initialize and sends initialized without failure cleanup. If either raises, construction fails without closing the selector or terminating and reaping the child. Wrap post-spawn setup in exception cleanup that releases acquired resources and re-raises the original exception; preserve live model defaults.
Use mocked process, selector, and transport objects with no network or real subprocess. Force initialize to raise TimeoutError while the fake child remains running. Assert selector closure, child termination and wait, and propagation of the same exception. Repeat with initialized send failure and with wait timing out to verify kill and final wait. The defect claim is falsified if the existing constructor already performs this cleanup in these cases; the fix fails if cleanup is omitted or masks the original exception.
Cleanup can itself raise or encounter partially initialized state. Guard each acquired resource and preserve the initiating failure. No claim is made that every initialization failure leaves a running child.

events.title: Honor the remaining RPC timeout
events.body:
Critic pass: call() already uses an absolute deadline, so adding another deadline would be redundant. Revised proposal: replace max(0.1, deadline - time.monotonic()) with max(0, deadline - time.monotonic()) when calling read(). The current 100 ms minimum can extend a nearly expired call. Preserve all live model defaults.
Use a fake process with recording stdin and silent stdout, a fake monotonic clock starting at zero, and a fake selector that advances that clock by its requested wait and returns no events. Make stdin.flush() advance time by 40 ms. Call with timeout=50 ms. Assert TimeoutError, a selector wait of approximately 10 ms, and final fake time approximately 50 ms. The current code instead waits 100 ms and reaches approximately 140 ms. No subprocess or network is needed.
Not executed; conclusions follow only from the supplied source. This bounds the requested read wait, not blocking writes or operating-system scheduling. The claim is falsified if the unchanged code passes this regression or the revised code still requests a wait exceeding the remaining deadline.

events.title: Clean up failed app-server initialization
events.body:
The supplied constructor creates a child process and selector before initializing the app-server, but has no cleanup path if initialization or the initialized notification raises. Revise the cleanup proposal to guard every resource acquired after spawning, including selector creation and registration. On failure, make a best effort to close the selector and terminate and reap the child, then re-raise the original exception. This is a source-backed reliability improvement; it does not establish how often the failure occurs. Keep live model defaults unchanged.

Ji An and the critic reach the same conclusion; their handshake and timeout cases strengthen the regression. The protocol critic identifies a plausible separate defect, but the supplied material does not establish 
Proposed offline regression, not executed: use fake process and selector objects. Independently inject an initialize timeout, an initialized-send failure, and a selector-registration failure. Assert that acquired resources are released, a running child is terminated and reaped, and the same triggering exception reaches the caller. Also simulate a wait timeout to check kill and final wait, and a cleanup exception to check that it does not mask the triggering error. A successful handshake must not trigger cleanup. The unchanged constructor should fail the failure-cleanup assertions.
Cleanup may itself fail or delay reporting, and partially acquired resources require individual guards. Best-effort cleanup cannot guarantee reaping when process operations fail. The proposals and test were assessed only against the supplied source; no code or tests were run.

events.title: Prioritize failed-initialization cleanup; correct the timeout regression
events.body:
The cleanup proposals identify the same source-backed gap: handshake exceptions escape after resources are acquired without explicit cleanup. They are corroborating interpretations, not independent experimental evidence. Revise cleanup to attempt each release even if another fails and preserve the original exception. The protocol proposal demonstrates response misclassification, but retaining a server request does not establish that it will be handled. Malformed-JSON diagnostics are reasonable; omit raw response content because even bounded excerpts can disclose sensitive data.
Use offline fakes to inject initialize failure and initialized-send failure separately. Assert selector closure, termination and reaping, and identity of the original exception; cover cleanup failure, wait timeout followed by kill, and successful initialization without cleanup. Correct the timeout proposal: call() establishes its deadline after send(), so advancing time during flush does not consume its timeout budget. Instead, advance a fake clock during delivery of an unmatched notification until only 10 ms remains, then assert the next read requests at most 10 ms. The existing 100 ms floor should fail this regression. No tests were executed.
The source supports missing explicit cleanup, not a claim that every failed initialization leaves a live child. Broader post-spawn cleanup must also cover selector creation and registration failures. Neither cleanup nor response validation establishes overall diagnostic reliability. Preserve existing live model defaults.

events.title: Validate response envelopes before matching RPC IDs
events.body:
Prioritize the protocol proposal: call() currently treats a server request with a matching id as a response and returns None. Require a dictionary, matching id, no method, and exactly one of result/error before accepting a response. Retain server requests through the existing unmatched-message path. The cleanup proposals are source-backed but duplicate one another; actual process leakage depends on child behavior. The malformed-JSON proposal improves context, but raw frame text is unnecessary and may expose sensitive content. The timeout proposal identifies a real 100 ms floor, but its test is incorrect: call() starts its deadline after send(), so a 40 ms flush does not consume that budget.
One deterministic offline regression: construct a client with fake send/read methods, sequence=0, and notifications=[]. Deliver {"id":1,"method":"example/request","params":{}} followed by {"id":1,"result":{"ok":true}}. Assert call() returns {"ok":true} and retains the request. The supplied implementation returns None on the first message. No subprocess, network, or real clock is needed. Test proposed, not executed.
The supplied source also permits unbounded unterminated frames, reports EOF without distinguishing a partial frame, and assumes decoded JSON has .get(). These warrant separate changes. A stricter matcher should define how malformed matching envelopes fail rather than silently waiting until timeout. No supplied protocol transcript establishes how often server requests occur. Keep live model defaults unchanged; no tools were called.

events.title: Clean up the child process when initialization fails
events.body:
The strongest minimal reliability improvement is to add exception cleanup around the constructor’s `initialize` call and `initialized` notification. The supplied source starts the child and registers its stdout before either operation, but a failure leaves no cleanup path. Preserve the original exception if cleanup also fails. Critic pass: this addresses a concrete resource leak; it does not by itself establish general diagnostic reliability. The malformed-JSON proposal is weaker because the raw `JSONDecodeError` already identifies invalid input. Timeout overshoot is concrete but bounded to the `read()` wait, while distinguishing server requests from responses depends on whether the server can reuse the client’s numeric ID—an assumption the supplied source does not esta
Proposed deterministic, offline regression: mock the process and selector, make initialization raise a known `TimeoutError`, and assert that cleanup closes the selector, terminates and reaps the child, and re-raises the same exception. Also make cleanup raise and verify it does not mask the initialization error. Separately inject failure from the `initialized` send. The decisive comparison is that the current constructor omits cleanup in these cases, while the revised constructor satisfies every assertion.
Cleanup must tolerate partial setup and an already-exited child, and must preserve the triggering exception. These are proposed tests only; no code was changed and no tests were run.

events.title: Prioritize failed-construction cleanup; correct the timeout regression
events.body:
Cleanup proposals have direct source support but duplicate one another. Cover all post-spawn setup: selector creation and registration can fail before the handshake. Cleanup stages must proceed independently if selector.close() fails, while preserving the original exception. The protocol proposal demonstrates matching-ID misclassification, but supplied evidence does not establish that the live server sends such requests; retaining a request also does not answer it. Malformed-JSON context is useful, but omit raw line content because bounding it does not prevent secret disclosure. The timeout proposal identifies a real minimum-wait issue, but its test incorrectly counts send time: call() creates its deadline after send() returns.
Use deterministic fakes without network or subprocesses. Inject selector creation, registration, initialize, and initialized-send failures; assert acquired-resource cleanup, attempted child reaping, and identical original-exception propagation. Make selector.close() fail and verify process cleanup still proceeds. Include handshake success and wait-timeout/kill cases. Correct the timeout regression by advancing the fake clock after deadline creation until 10 ms remain; assert read requests at most 10 ms. The existing 100 ms floor should fail this assertion. Test matching-ID server-request classification separately.
The final wait() after kill() is unbounded, so describing existing cleanup as bounded is inaccurate. Source supports missing explicit cleanup, not a guarantee that every failure leaves a live child. Literature metadata and prior outcome labels do not validate these changes. Tests were not executed; live model defaults should remain unchanged.

events.title: Honor the remaining RPC timeout; correct the regression fixture
events.body:
Replace call()’s max(0.1, remaining) with max(0, remaining). Critique: the earlier regression is invalid because call() establishes its deadline after send(), so advancing time during flush does not consume the timeout. The cleanup proposals identify a supported defect but duplicate one another; cleanup must attempt child reaping even if selector closure fails. The protocol proposal demonstrates a matching-ID request collision, but retaining a request does not handle it. Malformed-JSON diagnostics are reasonable, but should omit raw response contents to avoid disclosure. Preserve live model defaults.
Use a fake process with recording stdin, fake stdout, fake selector, and fake monotonic clock starting at zero. Initialize successfully with fake responses, then reset the clock and selector script. Call with timeout=0.05. The first select reports readability at fake time 0.04; fake os.read returns a notification plus newline. Subsequent selects advance the clock by the requested wait and return no events. Assert the notification is retained, TimeoutError is raised, the second wait is approximately 0.01 seconds, and final time is approximately 0.05 seconds. The supplied implementation instead requests approximately 0.1 seconds and ends near 0.14. A successful unchanged-code run would falsify this claim.
Proposal and regression were not executed; evidence is limited to supplied source. This removes the explicit timeout floor but does not bound blocking writes, scheduling delays, or processing of continuously buffered messages. Literature metadata supplies motivation, not validation.

events.title: Clean up failed app-server initialization
events.body:
Proceed with an isolated repair experiment. After the child is spawned, guard selector creation, registration, and the handshake. On failure, attempt selector closure and child termination and reaping independently, then re-raise the original exception. The supplied constructor has no explicit cleanup path for these failures. The critiques refine the proposal; they are not independent test evidence.
Using offline fakes, inject failures in selector creation, registration, initialize, and the initialized notification. Check that each acquired resource is released where possible and that the original exception propagates. Also check that selector-close failure does not prevent process cleanup, wait timeout triggers kill and final wait, and a successful handshake does not trigger cleanup. The unchanged constructor should fail the cleanup assertions. Tests are proposed, not run.
Cleanup operations can fail, and the final wait after kill is unbounded. Best-effort cleanup cannot guarantee reaping. This experiment does not establish failure frequency or overall diagnostic reliability; preserve existing live model defaults.

events.title: Approved
events.body: The change improves failed-constructor cleanup while preserving the original exception and leaving the successful handshake and model defaults unchanged. The deterministic, offline regression meaningfully covers all four initialization failure stages, independent cleanup failures, kill escalation, and success without cleanup. Limitation: mocked calls verify cleanup attempts, not actual process reaping; a second wait timeout can leave the child unreaped, as documented. Update the test docstring’s stale “not executed” wording to match the reported runs.

events.title: Approved
events.body: The change improves constructor failure handling: selector creation, registration, or handshake failures now trigger independent cleanup attempts while preserving the original exception. Successful initialization and live model defaults remain unchanged. The deterministic, offline regression meaningfully checks each failure stage, cleanup failures, timeout escalation, exception identity, and the successful handshake. Its evidence covers mocked cleanup behavior, not actual OS resource reclamation; a second wait timeout can still leave the child unreaped, as acknowledged. Update the test docstring’s stale “not executed” wording to match the reported runs.

outcome: The original failed the new regression, the candidate passed, and both reviewers approved.
